transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-02-11 | Start: 10:00 PST | Duration: 1:12 | Location: All-hands (virtual)
Attendees (on mic): Daniela Ortiz (CEO), Priya Shah (CTO), Marcus Lee (Head Product), Lena Park (VP Eng), Omar Reyes (Head People). Many others joined in view-only.

Summary:
Brief town-hall style leadership update focused on financial stewardship for H1, a temporary hiring posture, product prioritization (the sprint to narrow top bets), reliability investments, and a Q&A. The tone was candid; leadership asked teams to conserve runway while protecting customer-facing SLAs and core infra investments.

Topics:
- Financial stewardship and runway sanity checks
- Hiring posture and exceptions process
- Prioritization of product bets and roadmap triage
- Reliability soak and incident readiness
- Q&A: concerns on morale, comp, open roles, and private deployment demand

00:00 Daniela Ortiz: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We wanted to do a slightly different all-hands today — not the usual product demo but a clarity session, stewardship sprint, call it what you want. Short story: we are pausing on broad hiring growth and tightening spend across discretionary areas. We are not doing layoffs, this is a pause and triage.

00:34 Daniela Ortiz: I'll be very direct — market is tougher than last year, customers are optimizing spend, and model costs are up. Our purpose is to keep investing in what makes Redwood defensible: the serving runtime, reliability, and customer commitments. Everything else needs to be prioritized.

01:02 Priya Shah: Quick context from infra/tech — we ran a set of cost experiments in late Q4, some wins on batching & quantization, but the delta on cloud GPU pricing plus larger seq lengths for few large POCs means our unit economics slipped. We can regain ground by pushing caching, more aggressive quantization where quality allows, and some routing policy changes. We'll need product help to pick which workloads to optimize first.

01:30 Marcus Lee: On product prioritization — we're instituting a two-week sprint where we narrow the roadmap to top three bets. Those bets are: 1) host performance improvements (lower P95 latency), 2) Dedicated capacity automation and reliability, 3) developer experience for rollout/observability. Everything else gets parked or has to come with a kill-plan.

02:05 Lena Park: Engineering will reallocate two squads for the next six weeks to the reliability soak and kernel work. We'll do a 72-hour continuous soak next week to validate autoscale and failover. If you hear about folks being moved temporarily, it's part of that.

02:36 Omar Reyes: People update — we are pausing open reqs, but exceptions exist for critical customer-facing roles and hiring to replace attrition in key SRE/infra positions. We'll publish a clear exceptions rubric. Compensation and benefits remain unchanged; this is capacity management not cost cutting on people comp.

03:05 Daniela Ortiz: I want to emphasize the difference between a hiring pause and layoffs — we are protecting career growth broadly, but we need to be honest about where we invest. We'll have managers talk to their teams about scope changes.

04:00 (Audience chat has a few short reactions, applause emoji, and a question about whether Dedicated customers will be impacted)

04:20 Priya Shah: Dedicated customers are high priority. For those customers we will maintain capacity and SLAs; the triage is more on new feature expansion and some cross-team exploratory projects that are not directly tied to revenue or reliability.

05:10 Marcus Lee: There was a question earlier about Private/VPC demand — yes pipeline is strong, but those deals take longer, require security reviews (SaaS to private handoffs take time), and sometimes upfront professional services. We will continue to support but we are careful about custom engagements that create one-off maintenance.

05:38 (microphone flutters, snippet unclear) Speaker 5: — I think the ask is, how do we keep momentum on developer experience without broad hires?

06:00 Priya Shah: Good question. We will focus on automation and tooling that increases leverage: better observability dashboards, templated rollouts, and SDK improvements. Small teams can move faster if they have better infra.

06:35 Daniela Ortiz: Let's walk through a quick financial snapshot — high level: ARR growth slowed versus plan, cash runway remains healthy for the next 14–18 months under current plan, but there are lower and base cases where we want runway to extend to 24 months. Hence the stewardship posture.

07:15 Marcus Lee: Practically that means we will: defer non-critical marketing campaigns, reduce discretionary cloud spend (we're already reclaiming unused spot pools), and delay a large marketing event planned for Q2. Product roadmap: prioritize wins that show measurable unit-cost improvement or clear revenue impact.

08:02 Audience Q: Will comp cycles be impacted?

08:10 Omar Reyes: No, compensation cycles and planned reviews will proceed as scheduled. We are not deferring comp. Any change would be communicated well in advance.

08:35 Question from Eng: Are we freezing promotions?

08:41 Omar Reyes: No freeze on promotions. Performance progression is separate from hiring posture. If there are role or scope changes, managers should be transparent and partner with People.

09:10 (brief pause, someone types in chat with concern about morale)

09:24 Daniela Ortiz: Morale is top of mind. We know communications like this can worry folks. We will do regular syncs and AMAs — and leadership will be available for small-group office hours.

10:05 Priya Shah: Tech detail: we're targeting a 20% reduction in per-token cost for the top 30% of workloads within 60 days. Tactics include: better KV cache hygiene, more aggressive batching on batchy workloads, route low-prio traffic to cheaper variants, and exploration of int8 quantization where acceptable.

10:45 Marcus Lee: From product side we'll publish a triage rubric: impact on unit economics (tokens saved), customer revenue impact, and engineering cost to implement. If you have a proposed feature, submit it with those metrics.

11:20 (Audience poll launched: Which area should be top priority? Reliability, Cost, Developer DX, New Features — majority choose Reliability and Cost)

11:55 Lena Park: Reliability note — we had three incidents in Q4 with cascading scaling issues. Root cause analysis shows autoscaler coupling to instance warmup and certificate rotation timing. We're fixing the autoscaler logic and adding more chaos testing to avoid regression.

12:30 Speaker 7 (prod eng): Is the canary process going to change so small pushes can't create infra surprises?

12:45 Lena Park: Yes we'll formalize canary thresholds and introduce a 'blocking' metrics set that, if tripped, will auto-roll back or pause rollouts. More details coming in the canary handbook.

13:12 Marcus Lee: Quick words about Dedicated + private customers — we will keep the customer-facing SLOs; however some non-critical roadmap items that were planned to sweeten offerings will be delayed. Our sales teams will get a short messaging doc to explain this to buyers.

13:50 (background noise, someone coughing)

14:05 Q&A start (live questions from Slack and Zoom):
14:15 Q: How is this different from last year’s cost-reduction?
14:25 Daniela Ortiz: Last year was more surgical; this is broader prioritization but still with surgical exceptions. We are more proactive now — aiming to preserve runway without cutting R&D on core product.

15:00 Q: Will we still invest in new model support (multimodal, recent open models)?
15:10 Priya Shah: We'll continue to onboard high-value models that align with product bets and customers. Wide support for every new architecture won't happen — we'll be selective. If a new model materially improves cost/latency tradeoffs, it's a candidate.

16:05 Q: Are we changing the release cadence?
16:12 Marcus Lee: Short term, yes — releases with large new surface area will be delayed unless they are core reliability or cost improvements. Small, high-value fixes should continue.

17:00 (several quick comments in chat: 'thanks for transparency', 'can leadership share deck')

17:10 Daniela Ortiz: We'll publish the prioritized OKRs and the stewardship deck to the company drive by end of next week. The deck will include the exceptions rubric and the hiring guidance.

17:40 Omar Reyes: People team will host a live Q&A on Thursday for managers covering how to talk to teams, how to submit exception requests, and the process timeline.

18:05 (someone asks about customer renewals impact)

18:15 Marcus Lee: Renewals remain a focus — we are offering customers stability guarantees and migration assistance. For large renewals that require new features, we'll have a dedicated triage review with AE/SE and product to decide on reasonable concessions vs engineering cost.

19:00 Q: Any immediate changes to comp or equity?
19:05 Daniela Ortiz: No immediate changes. We want to maintain equity refresh cadence. If the macro environment forced different decisions, we'd be transparent. Today it's about prioritization.

20:00 (longer pause while a slide is shared — roadmap funnel visual, bars shifting)

20:45 Priya Shah: A technical aside — some of our quantization and kernel work will likely land in the open-source runtime we maintain; careful coordination is needed so enterprise customers that self-deploy can benefit but we also retain competitive differentiators. We'll communicate which bits are productized vs upstream.

21:20 Marcus Lee: On observability investments — we will make token-level cost charts, a per-route SLO dashboard, and a one-click rollback from the console. These are intended to reduce time-to-detect and reduce MTTR.

22:00 Audience question: Will support headcount be affected?
22:10 Daniela Ortiz: Support stays staffed to preserve SLAs. We may ask for temporary rotations to cover after-hours while other teams re-align.

23:00 (brief joke from someone in chat about 'stealth mode for budget')

23:20 Q: How do we measure success for the next 60 days?
23:30 Daniela Ortiz: Measures: maintain NRR (net revenue retention) within target band, improved unit economics for top workloads (20% per-token cost improvement target), zero regression in P95 user-facing latency, and clear published prioritized OKRs.

24:20 Priya Shah: We'll track a small number of heat metrics and publish weekly updates so the company can see progress.

25:00 (some cross talk, microphone lag creates overlaps)

25:30 Marcus Lee: Quick note for product folks: any roadmap ask needs a short template — impact in dollars or tokens saved, engineering hours estimate, and customer urgency. We’ll post the template after this call.

26:10 Lena Park: On reliability soak logistics — schedule will be next Tuesday at 18:00 UTC, please coordinate with infra pager teams. We'll post the runbook.

26:45 Q: Does this affect our partnerships or channel activities?
26:52 Marcus Lee: We'll deprioritize some co-marketing and channel pilots that are expensive; strategic partnerships with clear revenue upside remain.

27:30 (poll results are shared; majority support short-term prioritization)

28:05 Live Q&A continues — employees ask about team OKR alignment, manager guidance, and learning budgets.

28:35 Omar Reyes: Learning and development budgets will be slightly trimmed but we will preserve critical training and growth allowances. Ask your manager if you have a specific course or conference — exceptions will be evaluated.

29:00 (short silence while slides advance)

29:20 Priya Shah: We want to be clear about cadence: weekly leadership readouts on the triage progress; monthly all-hands updates for the company; and team-level standups for affected squads.

29:50 Audience question: How will this affect interviews and candidate experience?

30:00 Omar Reyes: We'll keep interviews going for approved roles. For non-approved roles we'll pause the loop and communicate to candidates. Recruiters have been briefed to set expectations.

30:30 (someone raises hand in chat asking about exceptions to hiring pause for AI research roles)

30:45 Daniela Ortiz: We'll consider exceptions for research if there's clear roadmap alignment and a path to revenue or stack leverage. Research asks must come with a concise plan.

31:10 Marcus Lee: On telemetry and observability — product teams should align on a small, open schema for cost metrics. We'll standardize tag sets so infra can surface meaningful dashboards.

31:45 Priya Shah: There's also a security note: private deployments will continue to get SOC 2 and ISO support, but professional services that require custom packaging will be evaluated case-by-case. We'll not abandon customers.

32:25 (audience murmurs, someone types: 'thanks for clarity on SOC2')

32:50 Short break while leadership share a customer story where reliability investment saved a major renewal.

33:20 Customer story snippet (recounted by Marcus): Last quarter we had a near-churn situation; fast triage by SE + infra and a targeted perf patch turned it around. That was the ROI of having a well-instrumented runtime.

34:05 Q: Are we still prioritizing open-source contributions?
34:12 Priya Shah: We'll be selective — contributions that increase leverage across customers or attract engineering talent can continue. Pet projects with little downstream impact will be shelved for now.

35:00 (someone mentions the need for clear cross-team ownership)

35:10 Daniela Ortiz: Ownership and SLAs are non-negotiable. If you need help defining ownership for a feature or metric, reach out to product ops.

35:45 Quick lightning round from each leader (1–2 minutes each):
35:50 Priya Shah: Focus on kernel work and caching, expect tactical RFCs.
:36:05 Marcus Lee: Product will publish triage rubric and OKR list.
36:20 Lena Park: Engineering will publish soak schedule and canary thresholds.
36:35 Omar Reyes: People will publish exceptions process and manager talking points.

36:50 Audience Q: How often will we revisit hiring posture?
36:58 Daniela Ortiz: We will re-evaluate monthly and share a clear signal for when we reopen.

37:25 (several questions submitted via chat that are addressed quickly)

37:40 Q: Will this change customer pricing or packaging?
37:48 Marcus Lee: Not immediately. We'll consider packaging changes that align with cost-savings and deliver clearer value (e.g., reserved pools with explicit latency windows). Any pricing changes would be discussed with sales and CSMs first.

38:20 Q: What about the roadmap item for new experimentation platform?
38:28 Marcus Lee: That goes to the park list for now unless it can show immediate ROI.

39:05 (more chat reactions and kudos)

39:30 Audience concern: hiring managers worried about losing candidates to competitors during pause.

39:40 Omar Reyes: We'll keep high-touch for prioritized candidates; recruiters will communicate proactively. We also encourage managers to be transparent during interviews about hiring posture.

40:10 Daniela Ortiz: Closing remarks — this is a stewardship sprint: short, focused, transparent. We will protect the things that make us Redwood: serving performance, reliability, and customer trust. We'll also ensure folks have clarity on expectations and paths forward.

40:45 Daniela Ortiz: We'll reconvene with a short update in one week and a fuller readout in four weeks. Expect the prioritized OKR deck by Friday.

41:10 Q&A wrap — final live question about morale: any immediate steps to boost team energy?

41:20 Omar Reyes: We'll do more small, regular check-ins, manager toolkits for 1:1s, and some social time to keep connections.

42:00 (some laughter, some applause reactions)

42:20 End of prepared remarks. Open floor for a few people to raise hands:
42:30 Speaker A (senior SWE): Quick suggestion — can infra productize a read-only token-cost dashboard for teams?
42:45 Priya Shah: Yes, we'll prioritize a small dashboard and a ticket template.

43:10 Speaker B (PM): ask: will the triage rubric be used to un-block paused projects?
43:20 Marcus Lee: Yes, submit using the template and we'll evaluate based on rubric.

44:00 (final wrap)
44:10 Daniela Ortiz: Thank you everyone. We're in a better place when we act together. Please review the deck when it's posted and bring questions to the manager AMA.

44:30 Recording ends; post-call follow ups include publishing the deck, the exceptions rubric, the hiring guidance, and the reliability soak runbook.

Recap (explicit next steps):
- Leadership will publish the prioritized OKR deck by 2027-02-18.
- People will host a manager Q&A on 2027-02-17.
- Engineering will run the 72-hour reliability soak starting 2027-02-18 and share results by 2027-02-25.

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker mislabels and a few dropped words during slide share; chat Q&A summarized inline.
